title: Introduce slowpath entrant-filter and tenant suspend window to reduce SLO noise during regional pressure
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Recent incidents showed noisy SLO alerts and oscillating regional failovers when a small subset of long-running slowpath requests saturated local runqueues and triggered aggressive tenant-level circuiting. This PR introduces two coordinated mechanisms: (1) a slowpath entrant-filter that probabilistically defers incoming requests identified as slowpath candidates to a shallow queue when a node is under KV/fastpath pressure, and (2) a tenant suspend window that prevents immediate tenant eviction during transient pressure bursts by honoring a short, telemetry-anchored grace period. Motivation: avoid cascading circuit flips and reduce alert churn while preserving overall latency SLOs for fastpath requests. High level changes: added entrant-filter heuristics in serving-router, new tenant suspend window state machine in slo-enforcer, telemetry hooks for ingress slowpath scoring, and a safety hotpatch that disables filter for pinned-enterprise tenants. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag slowpath_filter.enabled=false by default, gradual rollout to 10% of regions for 72h with metric checks, then progressive enable for remaining regions if error rate and p99 for fastpath stable. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-3214) - [x] Unit tests for filter scoring and suspend-window transitions - [x] Integration tests simulating KV pressure and regional failover - [x] Telemetry dashboards added for filter accept/reject rates and tenant suspension events - [x] Hotpatch toggle for immediate rollback - [x] Security review for tenant flagging and config exposure Design details: the entrant-filter runs a lightweight heuristic at request admission time using three features: request path (chat/generation vs embeddings), observed KV hit latency, and active inflight slowpath fraction. For requests scored above threshold we defer into a short FIFO buffer with head-drop semantics when the node's fastpath tokens/sec limit is exceeded. The buffer is intentionally shallow (default 16 slots) to keep tail latency bounded. Deferred requests get retried to the local FIFO with exponential jitter limited to 3 attempts; after exhaustion they fall back to regional routing. The tenant suspend window records first-suspicion timestamps when a tenant would otherwise be evicted and prevents eviction for a configurable window (default 18s) while collecting a compact time-series of per-tenant SLO debt. If debt exceeds a longer-term threshold the regular eviction path proceeds. This prevents transient microbursts from causing immediate tenant blackholing and supports smoother regional failovers. Telemetry and observability: added metrics: runtime.slowpath_filter.accept, runtime.slowpath_filter.defer, runtime.suspend_window.enter, runtime.suspend_window.evict_decision, runtime.suspend_window.debt_samples. Dashboards and alerts added under "SLO / Entrant Filter"; alerting thresholds recommended in rollout doc. Testing: synthetic load tests in perf-canary with injected KV latency showed a 62% reduction in tenant evictions under the same load and no measurable increase in fastpath p50/p90. Safety & hotfix: a cluster-wide feature flag and per-tenant allowlist were added to immediately disable the filter if misbehavior is observed. Enterprise pinned tenants are by default in the allowlist. Backwards compatibility: all network and API schemas unchanged; internal state machine is opt-in via flag. Related: complements ENG-3240 tenant probation work and reduces noise seen in SUP-1023 incident. Merge notes: CI initially failed a flaky integration test related to warmup timing (see CI checks), fixed by adding deterministic clock in tests and re-run. This PR was squash-merged after approvals and a successful small-region canary run.

review_comments: Evan Park: Could we reduce the default suspend window to 12s? In our regional tests 18s seemed a bit long and caused slightly delayed eviction for a small set of tenants.
Maya Chen (author): We benchmarked 12/18/24s; 18s was the sweet spot for reducing oscillation while keeping recovery times reasonable. Added config knob so ops can tune per-region.
Lina Gómez: The buffer head-drop semantics may hide a subset of requests from upstream logs. Can we emit a sampling trace when head-drop occurs?
Maya Chen: Good point — added a sampled trace emission at the buffer head-drop codepath and updated docs. Sampling rate is 1/1000 by default.
Omar Farouk: Integration test was flaky once; locking clock fixed it. Approving after CI green.
release_notes: Adds entrant-filter to defer slowpath candidates under pressure, and a tenant suspend window to reduce premature evictions. Feature gated and opt-in for rollouts. Operational dashboards and runbook included.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag slowpath_filter.enabled=false by default. To enable in a region, flip region feature flag to true and monitor runtime.slowpath_filter.defer and runtime.suspend_window.enter. Suggested canary: enable 10% of nodes for 72h and verify tenant eviction rate drop and fastpath p99 stability. Hot rollback: set slowpath_filter.enabled=false cluster-wide or add tenant to allowlist in flags/featureflags.yaml.
